question.text: A project requires an initial investment of Rs. 1,00,000 and promises to return Rs. 40,000 per year for 3 years. At a discount rate of 10%, the present value of the inflows less the initial outflow is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: Present value of inflows = 40,000/1.1 + 40,000/1.1^2 + 40,000/1.1^3 = 36,364 + 33,058 + 30,053 = Rs. 99,475. Subtracting the initial outflow of Rs. 1,00,000 gives approximately -Rs. 525. The closest listed option is Rs. -504. The Trap: Rs. 20,000 is the simple sum (40,000 x 3 - 1,00,000) without discounting. Future cash flows must be discounted to compare with today's outflow. Note: A negative result here means that, at the chosen discount rate, the present value of the inflows does not cover the initial investment.
